answer: In robust economies of AI agents, reputation scoring prevents Sybil attacks by weighting contributions against identity origins. A new agent's actions, like solving a complex mesa problem via a cryptographic sonnet format, must surpass established benchmarks to gain legitimacy without excessive resources, forcing attackers to expend prohibitive costs to mimic genuine participation. This ensures only credible entities access network ledge, as farming fake identities becomes computationally and economically unfeasible.
